title: The Rate Charged on a Catering Agreement That Keeps Pulling Orders
content:
An agreement that repeatedly pulls orders is charged on its record rather than on the notice it happened to give. Two counts decide the rate charged on a pulled order under a Corporate Catering Service Agreement: the cancellation charges standing raised inside the counting window, and the cancellations registered on the agreement in the 12 months ending on the day notice is given.

**Where 4 or more cancellation charges stand raised inside the counting window and 2 or more cancellations were registered on the agreement in the 12 months ending on the day notice is given**, the rate charged is the within-notice percentage printed against the catering service level whatever notice was given.

**Where at least 2 but fewer than 4 cancellation charges stand raised inside the counting window and 2 or more cancellations were registered in those 12 months**, the rate charged is the higher of the percentage the notice given yields and half — 0.5, that is 50 per cent — of the within-notice percentage printed against the catering service level.

**Otherwise**, the rate charged is the percentage the notice given yields.

### Cases on hypothetical figures

On an agreement whose catering service level is printed with a within-notice percentage of 60.0 per cent, so that half of it is 30.0 per cent:

| Charges standing raised inside the counting window | Cancellations registered in those 12 months | Percentage the notice given yields | Rate charged |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5 | 3 | none | 60.0 per cent |
| 4 | 2 | 60.0 per cent | 60.0 per cent |
| 3 | 2 | none | 30.0 per cent |
| 2 | 2 | 60.0 per cent | 60.0 per cent |
| 3 | 1 | none | none |
| 1 | 4 | none | none |

Both counts are tested together on each of the first two branches: 3 charges with only 1 registered cancellation falls through to the third branch, as does 1 charge however many cancellations stand registered. On the second branch the higher of the two percentages is taken, so a notice percentage above half the within-notice percentage governs and one below it does not.
